title: Compression
text: ZFP compressor built specifically numeric arrays. three lossy modes one lossless mode: Accuracy ("zfp-acc-[tolerance]"): value changes given absolute tolerance, "zfp-acc-0.001". Precision ("zfp-prec-[bits]"): Keeps fixed number bits precision, error scales value’s magnitude, "zfp-prec-16". Rate ("zfp-rate-[bits]"): Stores exactly given number bits per value, gives predictable file size, "zfp-rate-8". Reversible ("zfp-rev"): Lossless. ZFP requirements easy miss: needs 32- 64-bit numeric types: float32, float64, int32, int64. Inside Blosc2 ("blosc2-zfp-..."), float32 float64 work. h5lite automatically stores whole numbers smallest type fits (often uint8 uint16), integer data usually needs explicit . type isn’t supported, h5lite quietly uses gzip instead, check result h5_inspect(): can’t store NA, NaN, Inf. ZFP turn arbitrary numbers, h5lite writes data contains default pipeline (shuffle + gzip) instead. values come back exactly. Standalone ZFP compresses blocks one four dimensions. Data whose chunks dimension longer one (single value, say) four written default pipeline (shuffle + gzip) instead. hdf5lib 2.2.0.1 later, ZFP inside Blosc2 compresses chunks shape, stores data fewer four values uncompressed way. Blosc2, accuracy mode supports powers ten. "blosc2-zfp-acc-[tolerance]", tolerance rounded power ten (example, 0.05 becomes 0.01).

Native HDF5 Byte Shuffle (Fallback) standard compressor selected (e.g., "zstd-5" "gzip"), pipeline safely falls back core HDF5 library's native byte shuffle filter. guarantees improved compression maintaining universal compatibility. 4. ZFP & SZIP: algorithms perform mathematical compression directly numerical values corrupt bitstream rearranged beforehand. 1-Byte Data: Characters, booleans, 8-bit integers meaningfully shuffled, step skipped.

text: can read specific subsets n-dimensional dataset utilizing start count arguments. "Smart" start Parameter start designed intuitive. time, need provide single value. single value automatically targets meaningful dimension dataset: 1D Vector: start specifies element. 2D Matrix / Data Frame: start specifies row. 3D Array: start specifies 2D matrix. count parameter single value determines many units read sequentially. example, start = 5 count = 3 matrix read 3 complete rows starting row 5 (automatically spanning columns). Multi-Value start N-Dimensional Arrays need extract specific block inside structural unit, can provide vector values start. make indexing intuitive across higher-order arrays, start maps values dimensions following priority order, targeting outermost blocks first specific rows/columns last: N, N-1, ..., 3, 1 (Rows), 2 (Cols) example, 3D array, start = c(2, 5) targets 2nd matrix, 5th row. count argument always applies last dimension specified start. Dimension Simplification (Dropping) h5lite mimics R's native subsetting behavior regarding dimension preservation: Exact Indexing (count = NULL): provide start omit count, h5lite assumes targeting exact point index. read 1 unit drop targeted dimension. (e.g., reading specific row matrix return 1D vector). Range Indexing (count provided): explicitly provide count (even count = 1), h5lite assumes reading range. dataset's original structural geometry preserved. (e.g., reading start = 5, count = 1 matrix return 1xN matrix).

Mapping HDF5 Type Class: can target specific HDF5 data types using keys prefixed dot (.). Supported classes include: Integer: .int, .int8, .int16, .int32, .int64 Unsigned: .uint, .uint8, .uint16, .uint32, .uint64 Floating Point: .float, .float16, .float32, .float64 Example: = c(.uint8 = "logical", .int = "bit64") 3. Precedence & Attribute Config: Attributes vs Datasets: Attribute type mappings take precedence dataset mappings. specify = c(.uint = "logical", "@.uint" = "integer"), unsigned integer datasets read logical, unsigned integer attributes read integer. Specific vs Generic: Specific keys (e.g., .uint32) take precedence generic keys (e.g., .uint), take precedence global default (.).

title: Write an R Object to HDF5 — h5_write
code: file <- tempfile(fileext = ".h5")  # 1. Writing Basic Datasets h5_write(1:10, file, "data/integers") h5_write(rnorm(10), file, "data/floats") h5_write(letters[1:5], file, "data/chars")  # 2. Writing Attributes # Write an object first h5_write(1:10, file, "data/vector") # Attach an attribute to it using the 'attr' parameter h5_write(I("My Description"), file, "data/vector", attr = "description") h5_write(I(100), file, "data/vector", attr = "scale_factor")  # 3. Controlling Data Types # Store values as 32-bit signed integers h5_write(1:5, file, "small_ints", as = "int32")  # 4. Writing Complex Structures (Lists/Groups) my_list <- list(   meta    = list(id = 1, name = "Experiment A"),   results = matrix(runif(9), 3, 3),   valid   = I(TRUE) ) h5_write(my_list, file, "experiment_1", as = c(id = "uint16"))  # 5. Writing Data Frames (Compound Datasets) df <- data.frame(   id    = 1:5,   score = c(10.5, 9.2, 8.4, 7.1, 6.0),   grade = factor(c("A", "A", "B", "C", "D")) ) h5_write(df, file, "records/scores", as = c(grade = "ascii[1]"))  # 6. Fixed-Length Strings h5_write(c("A", "B"), file, "fixed_str", as = "ascii[10]")  # 7. Review the file structure h5_str(file) #> / #> ├── data/ #> │   ├── integers <uint8 × 10> #> │   ├── floats <float64 × 10> #> │   ├── chars <utf8[1] × 5> #> │   └── vector <uint8 × 10> #> │       ├── @description <utf8[14] scalar> #> │       └── @scale_factor <uint8 scalar> #> ├── small_ints <int32 × 5> #> ├── experiment_1/ #> │   ├── meta/ #> │   │   ├── id <uint16 × 1> #> │   │   └── name <utf8[12] × 1> #> │   ├── results <float64 × 3 × 3> #> │   └── valid <uint8 scalar> #> ├── records/ #> │   └── scores <compound[3] × 5> #> │       ├── $id <uint8> #> │       ├── $score <float64> #> │       └── $grade <ascii[1]> #> └── fixed_str <ascii[10] × 2>  # 8. Clean up unlink(file)

title: h5lite 2.2.0.0
text: Fixed R crash partial read variable-length strings failed (e.g. fractional start). start count must now whole numbers. Fixed writing data frame matrix column reading past end columns. Matrix columns, columns wrong length, duplicate empty column names now errors. R error raised mid-call longer leaves HDF5 file open (, Windows, locked) rest session. Strings marked "bytes" encoding now rejected writing starts. compression filter rejects data dataset closed (HDF5 flushes chunk cache) now error, incomplete dataset removed. Previously HDF5 dropped chunk silently. h5_move() longer deletes group moved (e.g. "g" "g/sub"); now error. Dimension scales (datasets holding names, dimnames, row.names) now kept consistent: h5_move() moves dataset’s scales , h5_delete() overwriting delete (scales named dataset, netCDF coordinate variables, detached kept), deleting scale detaches , writing scale never overwrites unrelated object (previously, writing x replaced anything named x_names, rewrite names moved dataset). h5_write(list, file, name, attr = ...) longer replaces dataset name group; lists can’t written attributes. List elements without unique, non-empty names now error instead dropped (, list(= 1, 2), deleting group). Overwriting group list now writes new group full removing old one, failure leaves original intact. POSIXct times now stored UTC (previously local times labelled Z), fractional seconds. POSIXlt now written like POSIXct instead empty group. Fixed-length strings fill full width now keep last character read files pad nulls spaces (h5py ). utf8[n] fixed-length strings longer truncated middle multibyte character, width measured UTF-8 bytes. = "ascii" now transliterates every string, just first. Values outside range requested type (e.g. 70000 float16, 2^63 int64) now error instead becoming Inf wrapping around. blosc2_truncate longer corrupts 32- 64-bit integers, including data frames (zeroed low bits: blosc2_truncate = 10, every int32 8192 read back 0), turns NA NaN Inf. now applies float32 float64 data without NA NaN. int64 NA values now read back NA instead -9.22e18, uint64 values int64 range read = "bit64" become NA (warning) instead clamped.

title: h5lite 2.2.0.0
text: Enum values matching member, attributes named like R’s structural attributes (dim, class, …), longer produce malformed reshaped results. Factors empty-string levels can longer written. Reading NULL dataset attributes longer errors. Lists can written root group (h5_write(list, file, "/"), h5$write(list)). h5_create_file() h5_open() now work read-files. fixes: unnamed (non-@ key) longer applies attributes writing; now honored factors (can stored strings, e.g. = c(grade = "ascii[1]")), raw, complex, integer64, NULL, nested lists; "skip" "null" must spelled rather abbreviated; type-class keys like .int match numeric data reading; "auto" keeps automatic type; attributes read written directly accept plain @ keys; "null" drops data frame columns reading. multi-value start data frame now error, start/count group apply datasets. h5_length() returns 0 NULL datasets attributes. h5_ls() h5_names() (groups) now return names order sort() puts , instead arbitrary order, full.names = TRUE returns absolute paths. h5_read() group h5_str() now follow order objects created (files written version; name order otherwise), lists read back order written. h5_str() shows names longer 255 bytes, h5_str() h5_attr_names() longer show HDF5’s DIMENSION_LIST/REFERENCE_LIST attributes. HDF5’s internal error stack longer printed h5lite’s error messages. h5_open() handle methods now accept arguments corresponding functions (e.g. h5$read(name, start, count)), ".." works absolute paths, relative file path keeps working setwd(). () around length-one POSIXct now writes scalar, warning longer objects appears . h5_inspect() reports filter parameters non-negative numbers.

title: h5lite 2.2.0.0
text: Fixed Blosc codecs without level ("blosc1", "blosc2", "blosc2-ndlz", "blosc1-snappy", standard "blosc*-lz4") "blosc2-zfp-acc-*" storing data uncompressed. "blosc1-gzip" "blosc2-gzip" now use Blosc instead plain gzip. ZFP float_rounding longer corrupt NA, NaN, Inf: ZFP falls back gzip float_rounding skipped data containing . print(h5_inspect()) reads Blosc2’s settings new layout well written earlier versions (including blosc2_truncate bits 1-D datasets negative settings) software, lists pre-filters order run (truncation, delta, shuffle), shows Blosc2’s ZFP codecs declined dataset. blosc2_delta blosc2_truncate longer passed "blosc2-ndlz" "blosc2-zfp-...", never ran . print(h5_inspect()) listed anyway, blosc2_truncate = 8 made NDLZ use 8x8 cells. print(h5_compression("blosc2-ndlz")) longer claims bitshuffle. blosc2_truncate must -51 52, 0. setting keeps bits drops whole mantissa used leave data uncompressed. float32 data, settings drop 23 bits skipped. "lz4-[level]" now passes requested LZ4-HC level instead always using level 9. ZFP tolerance rate 0 (e.g. "blosc2-zfp-acc-0", silently used tolerance 1) now error. float_rounding float16 bfloat16 data longer makes write fail; HDF5’s Scale-Offset filter can’t handle , skipped. compress = "none" longer chunks shuffles data, compress = TRUE now selects gzip instead compression. Unsupported data "blosc2-zfp-*" now falls back default shuffle + gzip pipeline. Standalone ZFP ("zfp-...") now falls back default shuffle + gzip pipeline data whose chunks dimension longer one (e.g. single value) four, ZFP can’t compress. write used fail. h5_inspect() longer prints large chunk dimensions scientific notation. Reorganized vignettes; vignette('compression') now covers every bundled codec, lossy compression, sharing files software, chunk tuning.
